description: Extensible formatting infrastructure for Portamical test data framework. Provides type-specific formatters, custom formatter registry, and zero-allocation string building for human-readable test case names and diagnostic output.
releaseNotes:
v2.0.0 (2026-06-27) - Architecture Simplification & API Refinement

      WHAT'S NEW:
      - Simplified formatter architecture (2 types instead of 3)
      - Single inheritance model via Formatter<T> base class
      - Flat namespace structure for better discoverability
      - Configurable maxCount parameter for Builder join methods
      - Enhanced XML documentation (60+ fixes and clarifications)

      BREAKING CHANGES:
      - Removed generic IFormatter<T> interface (replaced by Formatter<T> base class)
        • IFormatter<T> with contravariant 'in T' parameter removed
        • All custom formatters must now inherit from abstract Formatter<T> base class
        • Eliminates interface segregation - single inheritance model
        • Migration: Change 'IFormatter<T>' → 'Formatter<T>' and inherit instead of implement
      - Deleted CustomFormatters namespace and folder structure
        • Portamical.Core.Formatting.CustomFormatters.IFormatter<T> → removed
        • Portamical.Core.Formatting.CustomFormatters.Model.Formatter<T> → removed
        • All formatter types now in root Portamical.Core.Formatting namespace

      ARCHITECTURE IMPROVEMENTS:
      - Simplified formatter type hierarchy
        • Before: IFormatter (non-generic) + IFormatter<in T> interface + Formatter<T> base class
        • After: IFormatter (non-generic) + Formatter<T> abstract base class
        • Reduced complexity: 3 types → 2 types
        • Clearer design: Template Method pattern without contravariance complexity
      - Consolidated namespace structure
        • All formatting types in single Portamical.Core.Formatting namespace
        • Removed nested CustomFormatters/Model folder hierarchy
        • Improved discoverability and reduced cognitive load
      - Enhanced Formatter<T> base class
        • Now the primary and recommended way to create custom formatters
        • Sealed IFormatter.Format(object?) implementation ensures consistent type checking
        • Simplified implementation: override single Format(T) method

      BUILDER ENHANCEMENTS:
      - Added configurable maxCount parameter to join methods
        • JoinWithComma(items, maxCount) - default 3, configurable for different use cases
        • JoinWithSeparator(items, separator, maxCount) - flexible truncation control
        • Allows callers to control collection/tuple truncation threshold
      - Updated DefaultFormatter.Format(ITuple) to use maxCount: 8
        • Tuples support up to 8 elements natively before nesting
        • Ensures complete tuple formatting without truncation

      DOCUMENTATION OVERHAUL:
      - Complete XML documentation review and correction (60+ fixes)
        • Standardized all inline code tags: <ch> → <c> throughout
        • Corrected all class references: FormatterRegister → Formatter
        • Fixed all interface references: IFormatter<T> → Formatter<T>
        • Updated method references to Builder.* static members
        • Fixed cref attributes pointing to renamed/removed types
      - Enhanced API documentation
        • IFormatter: Clarified public visibility and usage patterns
        • Formatter<T>: Enhanced Template Method pattern documentation
        • Builder: Documented configurable maxCount parameter behavior
        • DefaultFormatter: Explained maxCount: 8 rationale for tuple formatting
      - Updated all code examples
        • Replaced IFormatter<T> with Formatter<T> in examples
        • Updated namespace references in sample code
        • Corrected registry usage examples (Formatter.* instead of FormatterRegister.*)

      CODE QUALITY:
      - Removed contravariance complexity
        • 'in T' variance eliminated - simpler type relationships
        • No more contravariant interface tests needed
        • Easier to understand and maintain
      - Improved test coverage
        • Comprehensive maxCount parameter validation
        • Tuple formatting with 4-8 elements tested
        • Updated CustomFormatterTests to align with new architecture

      MIGRATION GUIDE (v1.x → v2.0):

      1. Update custom formatter declarations:
         Before: public class MyFormatter : IFormatter<MyType>
         After:  public class MyFormatter : Formatter<MyType>

      2. Update namespace references (if using fully qualified names):
         Before: using Portamical.Core.Formatting.CustomFormatters;
         After:  using Portamical.Core.Formatting;

      3. Remove explicit IFormatter.Format(object?) implementations if present:
         - Formatter<T> base class provides this automatically
         - Only override Format(T value) in derived classes

      4. Optional: Leverage new maxCount parameter for custom formatting:
         - Builder.JoinWithComma(items, maxCount: 5) for custom truncation
         - Builder.JoinWithSeparator(items, sep, maxCount: 10) for flexibility

      5. No changes needed for:
         - DefaultFormatter usage
         - Format method signatures
         - Registry behavior or thread-safety

      BENEFITS:
      - Simpler API surface: Fewer types to learn and understand
      - Single inheritance model: Clear extension point via Formatter<T>
      - Flat namespace: Better IDE auto-completion and discoverability
      - Consistent naming: Formatter for both static registry and base class
      - Better documentation: Corrected and standardized across all files
      - Flexible truncation: Configurable maxCount for various use cases
      - Maintained performance: Zero-allocation formatting still intact

      FILES CHANGED:
      - Deleted: CustomFormatters/IFormatter.cs (131 lines)
      - Deleted: CustomFormatters/Model/Formatter.cs (258 lines)
      - Modified: Formatter.cs - Formatter<T> base class transferred, documentation updates
      - Modified: IFormatter.cs - made public visibility
      - Modified: Builder.cs - added maxCount parameter, documentation updates
      - Modified: DefaultFormatter.cs - uses maxCount: 8 for tuples, documentation updates
      - Updated: README.md - reflects new architecture and capabilities
      - Updated: Tests - comprehensive coverage of new features

      VALIDATION:
      - ✓ All builds successful (Debug/Release)
      - ✓ Zero XML documentation warnings
      - ✓ All unit tests passing
      - ✓ Backward compatibility in behavior (API signatures changed)
      - ✓ Performance characteristics unchanged
